
# Additional API Building Blocks (Clause)

`ogc.api.processes.part1.v1.clauses.additionalBuildingBlocks` *v1.0*

Complete published section of OGC 18-062r2, 1.0.0; modified BB rendition, not an OGC-approved publication.

[*Status*](http://www.opengis.net/def/status): Under development

## Description

<!-- Generated by scripts/extract_part1_v1.py; source SHA-256 1a1dcb80556dc054440fab25ef73c1535549c19e9e327877cf1c17f65007d32d. -->

<p class="source-citation"><a href="https://docs.ogc.org/is/18-062r2/18-062r2.html#toc58">Published source: OGC 18-062r2, 1.0.0 (toc58)</a>.</p>

<div id="additional-api-building-blocks">
<span id="toc58"></span>
<p id="_da298688-e677-77b9-bf34-fda0661d77e8">The core requirements classes of the Processes API standard are designed for the following workflow:</p>
<ol id="_f49ea80c-193a-1df8-aaf0-ea29fcde1d1a" type="1">
<li>
<p id="_ddaefbc8-ed47-d2af-21e6-d61a1a20b6c0">Access the list of available processes</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_fb110c13-b15d-d4af-3cd0-ff150bd1d149">Access the description of a specific process</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_b15e8a19-8332-2e80-93a1-c64dd66c122a">Create an execute JSON request (based on the description) and send it to the server via POST</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_0e93971b-98d9-a9c1-fe30-a1b0d0b3a227">Process the status info and/or results</p>
</li>
</ol>
<p id="_fa3e1984-aa0a-819a-b9be-533ab5237ccb">This workflow is useful for generic clients that are implemented against the JSON schemas and paths specified in this standard. Generic clients can communicate with any server implementing the OGC API — Processes Standard. However, there may be limitations regarding the handling of input and output formats.</p>
<p id="_8d3803e8-12ae-1972-af7f-b6b48b1e4577">The approach described above requires implementers of clients to have knowledge about the standard.</p>
<p id="_ce52fb8f-59db-fde8-c05d-96c3e1545164">This standard uses the OpenAPI specification to define the JSON schemas and OpenAPI MAY also be used to describe the concrete API (see <a href="#sc_api_definition">Clause 7.3</a>). A variety of tools for automatic code generation exist for the OpenAPI specification. This makes it very easy for client and server implementers to work with APIs defined using OpenAPI. However, as the OGC API — Processes Standard defines several JSON schemas and leaves the concrete data types for input and outputs open, the automatic code generation cannot be used to its full extent. To cope with this and thus make the implementation of clients / servers easier for those that are not familiar with OGC (API) standards, additional alternatives to the <a href="#sc_process_description">process description</a> and the paths to processes and jobs are permitted.</p>
<p id="_5a0d8523-cf28-e8db-f590-6d06328c7403">The following permissions do not affect the mandatory core requirements.</p>
<table class="recommend" id="per_core_alternative-process-description" style="border-collapse:collapse;border-spacing:0;">
<thead>
<tr>
<th class="recommend" colspan="2" scope="colgroup" style="vertical-align:top;">
<p class="RecommendationTitle">Permission 11</p>
</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td class="recommend" colspan="2" style="vertical-align:top;">
<p>/per/core/alternative-process-description</p>
</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="recommend" colspan="2" style="vertical-align:top;">
<p id="_de97a287-8b6a-223d-abf4-3bbb7371c558">Servers MAY support alternative means of describing the inputs and outputs of a process.</p>
</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p id="_c71a3b38-681e-6f80-e84b-7ec9d3379ed7">The alternative-process-description permission allows server implementations to describe a process, such as by defining the request and response body of a POST request to a process endpoint using the OpenAPI specification directly (see this  <a href="#example-alternative-process-description">example</a>).</p>
<table class="recommend" id="per_core_alternative-process-paths" style="border-collapse:collapse;border-spacing:0;">
<thead>
<tr>
<th class="recommend" colspan="2" scope="colgroup" style="vertical-align:top;">
<p class="RecommendationTitle">Permission 12</p>
</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td class="recommend" colspan="2" style="vertical-align:top;">
<p>/per/core/alternative-process-paths</p>
</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="recommend" colspan="2" style="vertical-align:top;">
<p id="_bc0de771-9aa4-5e8f-9360-5212c54ddbe3">Servers MAY support alternative API paths.</p>
</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p id="_fb17d837-fe30-9e34-d404-e824895636ab">The alternative-process-paths permission allows server implementations to specify alternative paths to processes and jobs.</p>
<p id="_26f1a6aa-7d10-803a-764f-7012ba0c5b94">An example of an OpenAPI document making use of these building blocks is shown in the following:</p>
<pre class="prettyprint" id="example-alternative-process-description">openapi: 3.0.2<br/>info:<br/>  title: Alternative OGC API - Processes<br/>  description: This is an alternative OGC API - Processes<br/>  contact:<br/>    email: you@your-company.com<br/>  license:<br/>    name: Apache 2.0<br/>    url: http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0.html<br/>  version: 1.0.0<br/>paths:<br/>  /buffer:<br/>    post:<br/>      summary: execute buffer process<br/>      operationId: executeBuffer<br/>      requestBody:<br/>        description: buffer inputs<br/>        content:<br/>          application/json:<br/>            schema:<br/>              $ref: '#/components/schemas/bufferExecute'<br/>      responses:<br/>        "200":<br/>          description: buffer created<br/>          content:<br/>            application/json:<br/>              schema:<br/>                $ref: '#/components/schemas/bufferResult'<br/>        "400":<br/>          description: invalid input<br/>components:<br/>  schemas:<br/>    bufferExecute:<br/>      required:<br/>        - data<br/>        - width<br/>      type: object<br/>      properties:<br/>        data:<br/>          maxItems: 10<br/>          minItems: 1<br/>          type: array<br/>          description: this is possible to provide the abstract in here<br/>          items:<br/>            oneOf:<br/>              - type: string<br/>                format: application/geo+json<br/>              - type: string<br/>                format: application/gml+xml<br/>        width:<br/>          maximum: 100<br/>          minimum: 1<br/>          type: integer<br/>          default: 20<br/>    bufferResult:<br/>      type: object<br/>      properties:<br/>        outputs:<br/>          type: array<br/>          items:<br/>            oneOf:<br/>              - type: string<br/>                format: application/geo+json<br/>              - type: string<br/>                format: application/gml+xml</pre>
<p class="SourceTitle" style="text-align:center;">Figure 28</p>
<p id="_4aa37249-471f-91aa-71ee-e5cf11874812">The goals of these additional API building blocks are:</p>
<ul id="_c21283f0-3632-fee7-f6fc-b8faa2276e25">
<li>
<p id="_39172243-2953-7ee5-64a3-78ccb0064ebb">Enabling a more seamless integration of this API with other OGC API standards and</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_bf4e49f7-978a-3806-a60c-9aaaced9736f">Enabling the use of tools to auto-generate clients / servers from the API description.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
